name: Handyman

pf.license.need: Set by each state's form, and sometimes the city's: none, a registration, or a home repair license. Many forms ask for one only above a job size they set.
pf.license.who holds it: The business, where the form asks. Each person only where the form licenses people. Lead-safe work needs a certified person on the job, where the rules require it.
what to ask: The company's home repair license or registration number, where the state or city has one
Each person's lead-safe certificate, for work that disturbs paint in an older home, where the rules require it
Insurance proof, where the form asks for it
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.job size limit: Where the form licenses work only above a job size, Rosie checks each job against it: at booking, when a task is added by text, and at the visit. Over it: only the part that fits is offered.
pf.license.jobs at one address: Where the form counts jobs at one address together, they're added up, so no job is split to stay under the limit.
pf.license.trade work: Electrical, plumbing, gas, heating and cooling, roofing and structural work need their own trade license. A handyman never books them.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks. A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that work.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the form asks for one.
pf.license.at the workshop: Repairs at the business's own shop: the form says if a license is needed. Safe default: the business registration on file.

pf.services.never booked: Electrical (light fixtures, switches, outlets, ceiling fans, hardwired smoke alarms, cords inside the wall), plumbing, gas, heating and cooling, roofing, structural work, work that needs a permit, and kitchen or bath remodels. The customer is pointed to the licensed trade, at booking or at the visit.
pf.services.several tasks: Tasks on one visit add up: their times set the visit's length, and their prices the job's total.
pf.services.capacity: One handyman per booking. A heavy mirror or a fence can need two. The workshop's clamp bench takes one furniture repair at a time.
pf.services.skills each needs: Fence work needs the fence skill. Lead-safe work needs the lead-safe certificate. Furniture repairs at the shop need the furniture skill.
pf.services.nobody home: Outdoor work with its own access, like gutters or a fence: nobody needs to be home. DONE comes with a photo. Indoor work needs an adult home the whole visit.
pf.services.online: A video check only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.materials: Anchors, screws, cord covers, patch and caulk are included. Other materials at cost with the receipt, agreed before work.
pf.services.guarantee: The owner's own (the example: 90 days on workmanship), shown on the receipt.
pf.services.aftercare: Re-caulking: keep the shower dry for about 24 hours. Re-glued chairs: don't sit on them for a day.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

stops the booking.words: Sparks, a burning smell, or a gas smell
stops the booking.says: Leave the house now and keep everyone out. Don't flip switches. From outside, call 911, and the gas company for a gas smell.
stops the booking.booking: No booking: it isn't a job for a handyman.

stops the booking.words: Someone hurt, or a ceiling or wall coming down
stops the booking.says: Get everyone away from it and call 911.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Keep people and pets away, and cover the window. If someone is cut, call 911.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A TV, mirror or shelf pulling loose
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Take it down with a second person if it's safe, or keep everyone away from it.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water dripping through a ceiling or a wall
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Turn off the water at the main shut-off, and stay away from outlets. That's a plumber's job first.

pf.safety.found at the visit: A hidden problem, like a soft wet wall, wiring or rot: the handyman stops that task, doesn't cover it up, takes a photo, and Rosie texts a written note saying which licensed trade to call. The booked tasks keep their price.
pf.safety.at the workshop: Broken glass is carried in taped and wrapped. Old furniture with lead paint isn't sanded at the shop.
pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

before the main visit.timing: On the secure page, before the booking is confirmed

before the main visit.timing: Before the quote; the owner picks which

before the main visit.for: Tasks that disturb painted walls in a home built before the year the rules set
before the main visit.timing: On the secure page before the visit, where the rules require it

before the main visit.step: A hardware match (the old hinge or latch brought in)
before the main visit.for: A special-order part at the workshop
before the main visit.timing: At least 2 days before; good for 3 months

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the handyman, with a photo. An adult stays home the whole visit for indoor work.
pf.visit.check-in at the workshop: The code at the counter (the handyman or the desk types it). A drop-off gets its code when the item is left, and READY when it's done.
pf.visit.before work: The handyman checks each spot against the booking photos. A different wall (plaster, not drywall) is a price change to the same task: priced and OK'd before drilling.
pf.visit.quotes at the visit: The handyman texts the quote with its lines before any work. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.extra work: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. Each added task must fit the state form's job size limit, as the owner confirms.
pf.visit.work sold at the home: A written right to cancel for tasks added at the home, where the rules require it. A price change to a task already booked isn't a new sale.
pf.visit.outside the license: A task that needs a licensed trade is pointed to that trade in writing, and the booked tasks go on.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The handyman texts DONE with the bill's lines, and after photos. Nobody home needed: DONE with a photo.

pf.money.materials: At cost with the receipt, agreed before work; bought after, they go on the bill.
pf.money.tips: Off by default; the owner can add a tip line to the bill.
pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the work.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies, as for every kind of work.

pf.messages.never in a text: Gate or lock codes, card details, and photos from inside the home: these stay on the secure page.
pf.messages.danger words: Sparks, a burning smell or gas always get the safety message first, before anything else.

pf.staff.levels: No person license by default. Each person's own license only where the state's form licenses people.
pf.staff.supervision: A helper works only with a handyman on the job. A helper is never sent alone by default.
pf.staff.special work: Lead-safe work only by people with the lead-safe certificate, where the rules require it. Ladder work over the plug-in's height only by people with the ladder skill.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs new customers' jobs, fees, quotes over the limit and same-day jobs. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another handyman with the same skill, at the same window and price.

pf.rules.job size limit: A license or registration above a job size, and jobs at one address counted together: from the state form.
pf.rules.written estimate: A written estimate or contract before work above an amount: from the state form.
pf.rules.right to cancel: A written right to cancel for tasks sold at the home: where the rules require it, with the days and the refund time they set.
pf.rules.words on papers: What the listing and papers must say, or must never say (like 'contractor' for a business without that license): from the state form.
pf.rules.lead-safe work: Lead-safe work rules for older homes: where the rules require it.
pf.rules.permits: Work that needs a permit isn't handyman work: it's pointed to a licensed contractor.
pf.rules.declared emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.guarantee: The owner's own (the example: 90 days on workmanship), shown on the receipt.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for handyman work:
handyman: A task that needs a licensed trade (a light fixture, a leak, a gas line): pointed elsewhere at booking or at the visit, in writing
A job over the state form's job size limit: only the part that fits is offered
A task added by text or at the visit: priced first, checked against the limit, and a right to cancel where the rules require it
The wall isn't what the photos showed: a price change OK'd before drilling
A hidden problem behind a wall (soft and wet, wiring, rot): stop, photo, and a written note
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A renter whose landlord pays or must OK drilling: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead
A TV or shelf pulling loose before the visit: the safety steps, then the soonest time
At the workshop: an item that can't be fixed, broken glass, or a drop-off nobody picks up

notes:
Pilot: home repair (the example: Ridgeline Home Repair, with its Ridgeline Workshop counter). Flow A: the customer brings a small item to the workshop counter (screen repair, door planing, latch or handle, drawer fix, storm window, chair re-glue, furniture repair, cabinet door). Flow B: a handyman goes to the home (TV mounting, door repair, furniture assembly, fence repair from photos, a repair walk-through).
Plug-in facts: photos, documents, firststeps, extrawork. Switches: cancelright on in flow B only (a fence or a job sold at the home with a contract: the master's B8-78 cancel window); sensitive, welfare and no2 off (the $2 is paid, D97). Settings: arrive setstart in flow A, window in flow B; cutoff 24 hours before.
Flow A money: list|card|counter (main; $35 screen repair, a card saved for the shop's $20 fee, paid at the counter), list|none|counter (nothing taken), list|full|none ($55 storm window repair, paid in full), photos|card|counter ($90 furniture repair from photos; card for $20; Sam OKs), visit|card|counter (cabinet door repair priced at the counter; card for $20; only the $25 consult promised). No holds.
Flow B money: list|card|bill (main; $179 TV mounting; a card saved for the $89 trip fee; the bill after the job), list|none|bill ($179, nothing taken), list|card|card ($179, the card charged when DONE), visit|card|bill and visit|none|bill (door repair priced at the visit; the $89 trip fee on a card), photos|deposit|bill (fence repair from photos, $640: $160 deposit once the quote is OK'd, $480 rest on the bill; $89 fee), list|full|none ($150 furniture assembly, paid in full). The $89 is the trip fee (the late-cancel and no-show fee).
Removed in this refit: legacy money words ops (vary keys by price and before), the A7-13 and B6-03 money lines, the B8-58 "never sent now" line (sent now is not a fact here), the "$40 fee held" and "$89 held" wording (a card is saved instead), all dead off ops. Own steps kept (none new). Branches kept: "It can't be fixed" (A8-32), "Alex asks for another trade's work" (B8-22).
Licenses: optional wording, never checked by Rosie (D96); electrical work is for a licensed electrician (the business's own word where the state requires one).
Children: 'Yes: a child may be left' is off at the counter; the rating split 'No: named-only work' is off (every finished job asks a rating).
